question.text: A block of mass m rests on an inclined plane. For the surface of this incline, the angle of repose is 45°. Work out the friction force on the block, the net force acting on it, and its acceleration, when the incline's angle θ is set to (a) 30°, (b) 45°, and (c) 60°.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the friction force, the net force, and the acceleration of the block when θ = 30°.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the friction force, the net force, and the acceleration of the block when θ = 45°.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: Find the friction force, the net force, and the acceleration of the block when θ = 60°.

conditions: block of mass m placed on an inclined plane
angle of repose of the incline surface = 45°
incline angle θ is evaluated separately at 30°, 45°, 60°

figure.description: A block of mass m sits on the sloped surface of an inclined plane that rises from a horizontal base; the incline makes an angle θ with the horizontal, measured at the base of the slope. The angle of repose of this surface is 45°, and θ is then set to 30°, 45°, and 60° in turn.

solution.approach: Compare each angle to the 45° angle of repose, where μ = tan45° = 1, to decide if the block stays still or slides, then apply the matching friction law.

steps.text: The angle of repose is 45°, so the coefficient of friction equals tan45°.
For θ = 30°, which is less than the angle of repose, the block stays at rest: static friction exactly balances the weight component along the incline.
steps.equation: friction = mg sin30° = 0.5mg up the incline; net force = 0; a = 0

steps.text: For θ = 45°, equal to the angle of repose, the block is on the verge of sliding but still stays at rest.
steps.equation: friction = mg sin45° = mg/√2 ≈ 0.707mg up the incline; net force = 0; a = 0

steps.text: For θ = 60°, greater than the angle of repose, the block slides down, so kinetic friction now acts up the incline.
steps.equation: friction = μmg cos60° = 0.5mg up the incline

steps.text: Find the net force and acceleration for θ = 60° from the weight component along the incline minus the kinetic friction.
steps.equation: net force = mg sin60° − 0.5mg = mg(√3−1)/2 ≈ 0.366mg down the incline; a = g(√3−1)/2 ≈ 3.66 m/s² down the incline (using g = 10 m/s²)

final_answer.value: (a) θ=30°: friction = 0.5mg up the incline, net force = 0, a = 0. (b) θ=45°: friction ≈ 0.707mg up the incline, net force = 0, a = 0. (c) θ=60°: friction = 0.5mg up the incline, net force ≈ 0.366mg down the incline, a ≈ 3.66 m/s² down the incline

common_mistakes.text: Applying kinetic friction at θ = 30°, below the angle of repose, gives a negative net force of size 0.366mg (3.66 m/s² with g = 10), showing the block cannot actually be sliding there.
